In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of an instrument for the assessment of driving ability in dementia, and with the evaluation of the instrument in a sample of patients with dementia.
the evaluation and assessment of the ability to drive in persons with dementia and the evaluation of the safety of the car in cases of dementia.
the following questions: How do people with Alzheimer's disease perform in a driving simulator and how does their performance compare with that of healthy older drivers and younger drivers?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the driving performance of people with dementia is not as bad as previously assumed, but that the driving performance is still reduced and that this reduction increases over the course of dementia.
there is no clear evidence of an increased risk of accidents in drivers with dementia.
the current evidence base does not support the use of the MMSE or MoCA in the clinical assessment of driving ability in people with dementia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the assessment of fitness to drive in dementia is a complex issue that requires the involvement of a number of disciplines and a multidimensional approach.
the driving performance of persons with AD is not only influenced by cognitive deficits, but also by the severity of the disease and the type of dementia.
the driving performance is impaired in dementia, but not to such a degree as to warrant an immediate driving cessation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the risk of a crash is higher in people with dementia than in people without dementia.
we can use a single model to estimate the probability of a crash and the severity of a crash, which allows us to estimate the probability and severity of a crash simultaneously.
we have a new way to assess the driving abilities of older adults and people with dementia.
